clue.text: Advert over railway for something to eat

parts.note: a puff is a promotional plug or piece of advertising
over means finished, past

explanation.surface: A billboard above the railway line promoting a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaky layered dough is a foodstuff, so this is something you eat, a general description by example.

clue.text: Settlement is crowded, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for crowded is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: crowded means packed, full of people

explanation.surface: A town or village where people live cheek by jowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settlement' looks like a village; it is an agreement settling a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement between parties is an agreement or treaty, a synonym.

clue.text: Driver's warning was written up as expected

parts.note: a golfer driving off shouts a warning cry to people ahead on the course

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the word is set upwards, read in reverse

explanation.surface: A motorist's alert turned out just as anticipated.
explanation.walkthrough: The Driver is a golfer, not a motorist: golfers shout FORE to warn of an incoming ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To have predicted something is to have expected it in advance, a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Legal case that shows one's young?

definitions.text: Legal case that shows one's young?

parts.words: Legal case that shows one's young?
parts.note: a court action brought to establish who fathered a child, so it proves whose offspring they are

explanation.surface: A lawsuit that seems to prove someone is youthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows one's young' reads like revealing youthfulness; it means proving which children are one's own.
explanation.definitionFit: This lawsuit decides whether a man is the father of a child, establishing his offspring.

clue.text: Spades or clubs? With two queens one mysteriously makes tricks

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: two asks for the abbreviation of queen to be written twice

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A card player asking which suit, holding two queens, works magic with tricks taken.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game surface makes 'tricks' sound like bridge tricks; here they are magic.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard or magician performs magic by mysterious arts, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Lie about switching second test

indicators.note: switching tells us the two parts, read lie then about, change places

parts.note: RE means about, concerning
to lie can mean to sit, rest in a place

explanation.surface: Fibbing about changing one's second exam attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie about' naturally reads lie first; 'switching' tells you to put the two parts the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking an exam again after failing is a second attempt, a definition by description.

clue.text: He wrote notes maybe covering for elder, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us the word for the tree covering is spoken, sounding like the answer

parts.note: the elder is a tree, and its outer covering is bark

explanation.surface: Someone writing memos, perhaps to cover for an older colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elder' looks like an older person; it is the elder tree. The sound match works in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian, the German Baroque composer, wrote musical notes, a cryptic hint at his work.

clue.text: Someone following in Model T, so parked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the found letters read upwards, in reverse
in signals the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A passenger in an old Ford car that has just parked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ELTSOPA, the letters inside 'Model T, so parked', back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple of Christ, or any devoted follower of a cause, is a follower.

clue.text: Haul new plastic nets, getting unexpectedly lucky

parts.note: to heave is to haul or drag

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the word nets is reshaped

explanation.surface: Fishermen land a catch in plastic nets and strike lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' looks like the nets' material but is the anagram signal, making SENT from NETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arriving as if from providence comes as an unexpected stroke of good fortune.

clue.text: Guardian article used in court worried Republican

indicators.note: worried means harried or shaken about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece used in court has a Republican anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper; it is a keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum keeper looks after a collection, so is its custodian or keeper.

clue.text: Marine guards Queen, returning debt that will grow massively

indicators.note: guards means encloses, so the word for marine goes around the rest

parts.note: marine means of the sea

indicators.note: returning means the note of debt is read backwards

parts.note: an IOU is a written acknowledgement of debt

explanation.surface: A Royal Marine protecting the monarch as she comes back with an unpaid bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian redwood is a tree that grows to colossal size, a cryptic description.

clue.text: No.1 mounts, kept by trained equestrian in form

indicators.note: kept by means held inside the rearranged rider's letters
trained means schooled into new shape, so the word equestrian is rearranged
in a down clue, mounts means climbs, so No.1 reads upwards

parts.note: NO is number and 1 is the letter I

explanation.surface: The top rider mounts horses kept by a schooled equestrian in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' suggests fitness or a horse's racing record; here it is a document to fill in.
explanation.definitionFit: A form is a printed sheet of questions to fill in, a synonym.

clue.text: Play in the traffic?

parts.note: a drama staged outdoors on public roads, played among passers-by

explanation.surface: A warning against children running into the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a child's game; it is a drama performed outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Performances given in public outdoor spaces rather than a theatre happen on roads and pavements.

clue.text: Rash devil dials mistakenly

indicators.note: mistakenly means wrongly, so the letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A demon dialling the wrong number.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash or reckless action is one taken unwisely, a synonym.

clue.text: Daily withdrawals of liquidity from the banks?

definitions.text: Daily withdrawals of liquidity from the banks?

parts.words: Daily withdrawals of liquidity from the banks?
parts.note: the sea pulls back from the shore twice a day, so water drains from the banks

explanation.surface: A financial report on banks running short of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquidity' and 'banks' look financial; they are water and shores.
explanation.definitionFit: The ebb of the sea leaves water at its shallowest each day, retreating from the shore.

clue.text: While touring at that time one sees old city

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for while encircles the rest

parts.note: as can mean while
then means at that time

explanation.surface: A tourist visiting an ancient city on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek capital is one of the world's oldest cities, with ancient remains.

clue.text: Orderly officer, that man needs payment!

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
he means that man
rent is a regular payment

explanation.surface: An army orderly complains that his officer owes him money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like a soldier's attendant; it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something orderly or logically arranged is clear and consistent, a synonym.

clue.text: Every one of the old revolutionary Southern ways

parts.note: all means every one

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the old form of the is read backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: All the old revolutionary traditions of the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow lanes or passages between buildings are routes, paths or ways.

clue.text: Needing pounds not pence, steals jewellery items

indicators.note: needing introduces the letter that comes in as a replacement
not marks the letter that goes out in the swap

parts.note: to pocket is to steal
L, from libra, is the abbreviation for pounds

explanation.surface: A thief wants big money, not small change, from stolen jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: P becomes L in POCKETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hinged pendants worn on a chain are pieces of jewellery, a definition by category.

clue.text: Slough introduced to exotic tango — this goes downhill fast

indicators.note: introduced to means put inside the rearranged dance
exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters of tango are rearranged

parts.note: a slough is a swamp or bog

explanation.surface: The Berkshire town of Slough discovers the tango, which soon goes downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is an English town, but here a slough is a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled for sliding down snowy slopes travels rapidly downhill, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Gear Ruby argued occasionally is junk

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only alternate letters are used

explanation.surface: Ruby claimed now and then that the equipment was rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish, trash and junk are synonyms for unwanted waste.

clue.text: Gadget that makes space less polluted?

definitions.text: Gadget that makes space less polluted?

parts.words: Gadget that makes space less polluted?
parts.note: the device is named after empty space, and it makes rooms cleaner

explanation.surface: A device to clean up outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: A vacuum is empty space, so its 'cleaner' sounds like a cosmic purifier; it is a household appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hoover-type appliance sucks up dust from carpets, a domestic machine.

clue.text: What may be stuffed in banger, say, before function

parts.note: a banger is British slang for an old, battered car
to go means to function or work

explanation.surface: A sausage stuffed before cooking, as a culinary function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' looks like a sausage; it is British slang for an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or freight are loaded into a vehicle, ship or plane, stuffed in for transport.

clue.text: Bill the headmaster

definitions.meaning: old British school slang for a headmaster or schoolmaster

explanation.surface: A teacher named Bill runs the school.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's bill is its hard pointed mouth, and British schoolboy slang called a headmaster this too.

clue.text: Woolly middle in peppers we ate roasted

indicators.note: middle in means the letters sit in the middle of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A soft, vague centre in the roasted peppers we had for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolly' looks like an adjective; it is a noun, a knitted top.
explanation.definitionFit: A woolly is British informal for a knitted pullover, a synonym.

clue.text: Move abroad — good to get away somewhere in the Gulf?

indicators.note: to get away means to leave, so the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: to emigrate is to move abroad

explanation.surface: Relocating overseas to escape to the Persian Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai and Abu Dhabi are states ruled by a sheikh on the Persian Gulf, an example.

clue.text: Cinders put on diamonds showing sparkle

indicators.note: put on means placed after, so the ashes follow the card suit

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
cinders are ash

explanation.surface: Cinderella puts on her diamonds and shines at the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cinders' looks like Cinderella; it is burnt remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash means flair, panache or sparkle, a synonym for style.

clue.text: Hold-up requires audacity and impudence

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
neck is British slang for cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: A robbery demands nerve and cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up' looks like a robbery; it is a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow point where traffic or progress jams causes a delay.
